A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProbeX and tree-expert research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-weight classification, text-alignment, retrieval, and one-class classification experiments, plus ablations and model-repository analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds transfer experiments, DINO results, sensitivity analyses, and additional retrieval examples.

M1.justification: The specified nearest-center router changes from L1 distance in v1 Equation 1 to L2 distance in v2 Equation 5. ProbeX's learned probes, shared projection, nonlinear probe encoders, aggregation, prediction head, and training objectives remain substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: Model-J adds a DINO-derived input-model population. v2 also reports preliminary text-alignment experiments on discriminative models, extending that evaluation beyond Stable Diffusion. The underlying CIFAR100/ImageNet coverage and principal classification and retrieval tasks are retained.

E2.justification: The principal benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. v2 adds a shared-predictor comparison against tree experts in Figure 3d and reports near-random Neural Graphs trials without tabulated scores. Dense is absent from the replacement dataset-size comparison in Figure 14, whereas v1 Table 8 compared Dense with ProbeX.

E3.justification: Reported ProbeX dimensions change from 10% of the corresponding layer dimensions to fixed rU=rV=rT=128. The MAE population increases from 500 to 1,000 models. New experiments introduce controlled tree mixing and broader dimension, depth, and sample-size sweeps. The 70/10/20 split and 500-epoch budget are retained; the PDFs do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds within-tree and cross-tree transfer controls, dimension ablations, SD200 layer rankings, dataset-quality analyses, and additional non-cherry-picked retrieval examples. Depth curves quantify v1's preliminary observation about deeper encoders, and the dataset-size analysis expands substantially. Existing ReLU and text-encoder ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Seed annotations on the illustrated retrieval models change: the first retrieved model has seed 42 in v1 Figure 6 and seed 0 in v2 Figure 7, with other seed labels also revised. These are limited changes to seed information, not evidence of additional evaluation runs. Neither version reports repeated-run counts or uncertainty intervals.

E6.justification: Discriminative results and capacities are revised: for example, ResNet ProbeX changes from 0.800 accuracy with 366k parameters to 0.842 with 2.3m parameters. The motivating intra-tree accuracy changes from 0.940 to 0.844, but v2 inconsistently identifies its architecture as ResNet9 in text and ViT in Figure 3, preventing a controlled comparison. DINO, transfer, and appendix results are added; the main SD alignment and kNN/OCC scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The dense-versus-linear-probing equivalence and Tucker-factorization propositions retain the same assumptions and constructive proofs in Appendix A. Their revised wording, notation, and equation numbering introduce no substantive theoretical development.

C1.justification: v2 centers training-category prediction, explicitly claims state-of-the-art results for that task, and confines its headline language-alignment claim to Stable Diffusion. The central contributions of tree-wise learning, efficient single-layer ProbeX, and zero-shot weight classification remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds an important applicability limitation: text alignment on discriminative models works in distribution but fails on unseen classes. Section 8 hypothesizes that Stable Diffusion's cross-attention facilitates alignment. New layer-ranking and capacity analyses also add substantive interpretations. The earlier unseen-tree limitation and mechanistic/self-supervised discussions are retained, partly in Appendix B.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information through dataset-generation hyperparameter tables, root-checkpoint identifiers, LoRA rank, prompt templates, optimizer settings, clustering implementation details, and baseline adaptations. It also adds a project link and documents the repository-analysis source and date. Most additions disclose previously unspecified details rather than establish changes to the underlying experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations concerning deep linear probe generators, model zoos, weight-space clustering, and model merging. Appendix G explicitly contrasts Model-J with small, randomly initialized model collections. The latent-optimization and Tucker references are removed, while the broad related-work framework remains.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper and substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, motivation, and method exposition. Section 4 derives ProbeX before presenting routing, while experimental settings and parts of the discussion move into expanded appendices. This substantially changes narrative organization beyond the insertion of new results.

P2.justification: The motivating table becomes the four-panel Figure 3, retrieval and tree-size diagrams are redrawn, and dataset and text-encoder tables move to the appendix. New ablation plots, layer-ranking and hyperparameter tables, distribution plots, and retrieval panels substantially expand and reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important weaknesses in v1's empirical support for tree-wise learning and its sparse reproduction information. Transfer controls, capacity and depth analyses, and detailed dataset-generation and implementation disclosures make the approach substantially easier to assess and reproduce. The newly stated discriminative-alignment failure also improves claim calibration. Figure 3's architecture inconsistency limits one comparison, but the gains in evidence, transparency, and applicability guidance outweigh that reporting defect.
